messages:
anya: quick heads-up — ran a stability probe across a handful of us-west-2 GPU nodes using the DCGM exporter. Seeing clusters of ECC/Xid spikes that affect multiple cards on the same node within a ~2m window. Not isolated single-card flake, looks correlated.

mike: can you paste a short example of the metric and a grep output? curious if it's the same GPU_UUID or same PCI slot pattern.

anya: sure, this is what i'm seeing from a quick scrape:
```
$ curl -s http://dcgm-exporter.node:9400/metrics | grep dcgm_ecc | head -n 6
dcgm_ecc_errors_total{gpu_uuid="GPU-aaa111",gpu_index="0",node="node-23"} 12
dcgm_ecc_errors_total{gpu_uuid="GPU-bbb222",gpu_index="1",node="node-23"} 9
dcgm_ecc_errors_total{gpu_uuid="GPU-ccc333",gpu_index="2",node="node-23"} 11
```
All three incremented within ~90s. Xid logs on the node show similar timestamps.

jules:ooooo that's interesting — sounds like a node-level environmental issue (power/PCI/BIOS) or kernel driver hiccup causing multiple cards to misbehave at once. For alerting, current rules fire per-card which causes churn and premature drains. We should group and debounce by node-level cardinality.

mike: +1. Proposed quick recording rule to count recently failing GPUs on a node:
```yaml
# recording rule (prometheus)
- record: node:gpu_unhealthy_count:sum
  expr: sum by(node)(increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 0)
```
Then alert if node:gpu_unhealthy_count:sum >= 2 for 15m. That avoids single-card auto-drains.

liam: minor tweak: use `count_over_time` or `sum_over_time` to avoid Prometheus boolean coercion oddities. Also add a probation window to ignore very new cards (first 10m after boot) to avoid false positives from driver init churn. e.g.:
```yaml
# probation label-based exclusion (pseudo)
expr: sum by(node)(increase(dcgm_ecc_errors_total[5m]) > 0 and (time() - node_gpu_boot_seconds > 600))
```
We don't have node_gpu_boot_seconds yet; we can export a small cosmetic metric from node-exporter / custom script to mark GPU runtime.

jules: also consider correlating with `dcgm_power_violation` / `dcgm_temperature` metrics — if temps/power on that node spike concurrently that's a different class of failures (cooling or PSU).

anya: agreed. My doc notes: prioritize grouping by `node` and `gpu_uuid` first, then add correlation scoring across thermal/power metrics. For short-term ops: change alert severity to P2 for node-level 1-card events, P1 only when >=2 cards or recurring Xid > 3 within 30m. That will cut noisy escalations.

sre-bot: ALERTS: dcgm-ecc-card-firing node-23 gpu-0 (3 times in 5m)
sre-bot: ALERTS: dcgm-ecc-card-firing node-23 gpu-1 (2 times in 5m)

mike: playbook change proposal: instead of immediate `kubectl drain`, do `kubectl cordon` + schedule a maintenance job to repro the failure with `stress-ng` + `nvidia-smi --query` health checks. If multiple cards fail, then escalate to drain+replace. This avoids unnecessary pipeline disruption.

anya: testing plan: push a Prometheus rule change to staging to evaluate false positive rate for 48h, run probe that simulates single-card noise and multi-card correlated faults, and measure how often node-level alert triggers. If <5% FP, roll to prod.

deploy-bot: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/+/pr/1234 (prometheus: add node:gpu_unhealthy_count + new alert grouping). scheduled deploy to staging tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

liam: can we also log the PCIe bus errors from dmesg in the node event when an alert fires? a small `node-exporter` textfile collector could capture `/var/log/kern.log` tail for Xid lines. Helps hardware triage.

jules: yes — add to runbook: copy dmesg snippet + snapshot `nvidia-smi -q` and attach to the incident ticket. If thermal/power correlation present, open a hardware replacement request.

anya: thanks all — i'll push the staging rule and run the probe tomorrow. tagging @mike @jules for review on the probation metric approach. :thumbsup:

mike: lgtm, will review PR tonight.

jules: ack, will prepare hardware triage checklist.

sre-bot: note: scheduled alerting experiment (id: probe-2026-03-19) will start at 03:00 UTC.

anya: leaving notes in ops-runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/gpu-health/probes (will add outcomes after the test).
